t: You're looking at the monument to General William Booth and his wife Catherine, in Abney Park Cemetery in Hackney. Together they founded the Salvation Army, a Christian movement begun in 1865 that has spread from London to many parts of the world. William became its first General and served until 1912. Catherine, who died in 1890, was known as the Mother of the Salvation Army, because of her influence in shaping it. The Army's quasi-military structure and its humanitarian work are what the couple are remembered for, and this monument commemorates them both.
